newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RTRS-Cricket-Tufnell ties down NZ with four wickets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket-Tufnell ties down NZ with four wickets.

text.p: England spinner Phil Tufnell bounced back from an off-field controversy to take four wickets on Thursday as his side restricted New Zealand to 222 for six in the first of five one-day cricket internationals.
Tufnell claimed four for 22 from 10 overs, his best one-day international figures, to slow down the home side after an aggressive, free-scoring start.
Earlier this week, England manager John Barclay rejected allegations by staff at a Christchurch restaurant that Tufnell and two companions had smoked cannabis in a toilet there.
New Zealand launched a brisk early onslaught, racing to 76 for one from 15 overs as Nathan Astle ripped into the England attack with a series of powerful off-drives.

After reaching 50, Astle gave Tufnell his first wicket when he caught a leading edge and lobbed a simple catch to Graham Thorpe. The England spinner added the scalps of Adam Parore, Stephen Fleming and Chris Cairns as New Zealand's middle order batsmen faltered after promising starts.
Captain Lee Germon and Chris Harris raised the tempo with a sixth wicket stand of 55, and Harris remained unbeaten on 48 at the close of the 50-over innings.

New Zealand, who omitted fast bowler Geoff Allott, won the toss and chose to bat in front of a capacity 25,000 crowd in the first day-night international to be played at the Lancaster Park ground in Christchurch.

England made one change to the team that won the third test, and the series 2-0, on the same ground two days ago. The tourists brought in left-arm fast-medium bowler Alan Mullally to replace Andrew Caddick.
